title: Phones, apps & payments
goal: Sort out the wi-fi, use apps and accounts safely, order online and track a delivery, pay by UPI (and deal with a failed payment), and talk about posts, reels and stories.
intro:
Tech talk in Hindi is mostly English words — *app, download, password, OTP, order, reel* — held together by Hindi grammar. The trick is knowing **which Hindi verb** goes with each one: you **डाउनलोड करते** हैं an app, but the app **डाउनलोड होता** है; you **पोस्ट डालते** हैं and **स्टोरी लगाते** हैं.

India also pays differently: almost everything, from a metro ticket to a cup of chai, is paid by **UPI** — scan the QR code, enter your PIN, done. This unit gives you the phrases for all of it, including what to say when the money's gone but the payment hasn't (**पैसे कट गए पर पेमेंट नहीं हुआ!**), and practises **if-sentences** the way people actually use them.

grammar.title: English word + Hindi verb: डाउनलोड करना or डाउनलोड होना?
grammar.body:
Hindi doesn't conjugate English verbs. It takes the English word as a **noun** and adds a Hindi verb — and which verb you choose matters.

**करना** when *someone does it* (transitive): मैं ऐप **डाउनलोड कर** रहा हूँ 'I'm downloading the app', फ़ोन **अपडेट करो** 'update your phone', **पेमेंट कर** दो 'pay', **लॉग इन करो** 'log in'.
**होना** when *it happens* (intransitive): ऐप **डाउनलोड हो** रहा है 'the app is downloading', फ़ोन **अपडेट हो** गया 'the phone has updated', **पेमेंट हो** गया 'the payment went through', फ़ोन **हैंग हो** गया 'the phone froze'.

This is exactly the same as Hindi's own pairs from unit 16 (तोड़ना 'break something' / टूटना 'break'). You can use it for any new word: *चार्ज करना / चार्ज होना*, *सेव करना / सेव होना*, *ब्लॉक करना / ब्लॉक होना*.

**In the past with करना, ने and agreement apply** — the verb agrees with the English noun's Hindi gender: मैंने ऐप डाउनलोड **किया** (m), उसने मेरी पोस्ट लाइक **की** (पोस्ट f), मैंने रील शेयर **की** (f).

**Some words take other verbs**, just as they do in English: पोस्ट **डालना** 'to post', स्टोरी **लगाना** 'to put up a story', ओटीपी **आना** 'to receive an OTP', नेटवर्क **आना** 'to have signal', फ़ोन **चलाना** 'to use a phone', ऑर्डर **देना** 'to place an order'.

**The trap:** ऐप डाउनलोड **करो** is an instruction to a person; ऐप डाउनलोड **हो** रहा है describes the progress bar. Don't mix them: *ऐप डाउनलोड कर रहा है* would mean 'the app is downloading something'.

grammar.title: If-sentences in real life: अगर … तो …
grammar.body:
Unit 19 introduced **अगर … तो …** 'if … then …'. In everyday speech it gets shorter and more flexible.

**1. Tense in the अगर clause.** For a future condition Hindi often uses the **past** (perfective) where English uses the present:
अगर ओटीपी नहीं **आया**, तो दोबारा भेजना 'if the OTP doesn't come, send it again'
अगर पेमेंट **हो गया**, तो स्क्रीनशॉट भेज देना 'if the payment goes through, send me a screenshot'
The **future** (आएगा) and the **subjunctive** (आए) are also fine: अगर पेमेंट **हो जाए** तो… The past makes it sound like 'once/in case that has happened'.

**2. Drop अगर.** The **तो** alone is enough, and this is how people mostly speak: नेट नहीं चल रहा **तो** कैश दे दो 'if the net's not working, just give cash'. पैसे कट जाएँ **तो** घबराना मत.

**3. Condition + instruction** is the commonest pattern: अगर … तो + imperative (करो, कीजिए, or the 'later' infinitive करना).

**4. Otherwise: वरना / नहीं तो.** जल्दी पेमेंट करो, **वरना** ऑर्डर कैंसल हो जाएगा 'pay quickly, or the order will be cancelled'.

**The trap:** in the अगर clause, **don't** use होता/आता for a real possibility — अगर पेमेंट नहीं **होता** is the *unreal* 'if the payment didn't go through (but it did)' of unit 36. For a real 'if', use हुआ / होगा / हो.

culture:
India runs on **UPI**. Every shop, auto-rickshaw, chai stall and vegetable cart has a printed **QR code**, and you'll hear **पेटीएम करो**, **जीपे कर दूँ?** or **स्कैन कर लो** far more than any question about cash. A sound box at the counter announces each payment out loud ('₹50 प्राप्त हुए'). Still, keep some cash: the network fails, and small vendors may not have change (**छुट्टा**).

Food and groceries come through apps — Zomato, Swiggy, Blinkit, Zepto — often in ten minutes, and the delivery rider will **call** you rather than ring the bell: **भैया, लोकेशन भेज दो** or **नीचे आ जाइए**. You call them **भैया** too. Scams are common: the 'KYC update' call, the 'I sent you money by mistake, please return it' message, the fake link. Golden rule: **ओटीपी और पिन किसी को मत बताना** — no bank or company will ever ask.

Online, most people write Hindi in the **Roman alphabet** (*kya kar rahe ho?*, *bhai party kab hai*), mixed freely with English. Family **WhatsApp groups** are their own world of 'good morning' images and forwards, while younger people live on Instagram reels and stories. Data is cheap, so video calls and endless reels are normal — and **नेट नहीं चल रहा** is a universal excuse.

tip.title: English word + करना or होना
tip.body:
- English tech words are nouns; add a Hindi verb.
- **करना** when someone does it: फ़ोन **हैंग कर** दिया 'you made it freeze'.
- **होना** when it just happens: फ़ोन **हैंग हो** गया 'it froze', डेटा **ख़त्म हो** गया.
- In the ने past the verb agrees with the noun: पासवर्ड (m) बदल **दिया**.
tip.pattern: X करना (someone does it)  ·  X होना (it happens)

tip.title: OTPs, links and scams
tip.body:
- **ओटीपी** and **पिन** are never shared: ओटीपी किसी को **मत बताना**.
- Strange link? लिंक **मत खोलना**. That's a **फ़्रॉड**.
- Same verb rule: ऐप डाउनलोड **करो** (you), ऐप डाउनलोड **हो** रहा है (it).
- ओटीपी **आता** है — you 'receive' it with आना: ओटीपी नहीं **आया**.

sentences.en: Download this app, it's really useful.

sentences.en: The app's downloading, one minute.

sentences.en: I updated the app last night.

sentences.native: ओटीपी नहीं आया, फिर से भेजो।
sentences.roman: oṭīpī nahīṃ āyā, phir se bhejo.
sentences.en: The OTP didn't come, send it again.

sentences.native: ओटीपी और पिन किसी को मत बताना, बैंक वाले भी नहीं माँगते।
sentences.roman: oṭīpī aur pin kisī ko mat batānā, baiṅk vāle bhī nahīṃ māṃgte.
sentences.en: Don't give your OTP or PIN to anyone — even the bank never asks for them.

sentences.native: मैं अपने अकाउंट में लॉग इन नहीं कर पा रहा।
sentences.roman: maiṃ apne akāunṭ meṃ log in nahīṃ kar pā rahā.
sentences.en: I can't log in to my account.

sentences.native: यह फ़्रॉड है, यह लिंक मत खोलना!
sentences.roman: yah froḍ hai, yah liṅk mat kholnā!
sentences.en: It's a scam — don't open that link!

sentences.native: लिंक भेज दो, मैं देख लूँगा।
sentences.roman: liṅk bhej do, maiṃ dekh lūṃgā.
sentences.en: Send me the link, I'll have a look.

sentences.native: मेरे साथ फ़्रॉड हो गया, पाँच हज़ार रुपये गए।
sentences.roman: mere sāth froḍ ho gayā, pāṃch hazār rupaye gaye.
sentences.en: I got scammed — five thousand rupees gone.

sentences.native: खाना बनाने का मूड नहीं है, ऑनलाइन मँगवा लेते हैं।
sentences.roman: khānā banāne kā mūḍ nahīṃ hai, onlāin maṃgvā lete haiṃ.
sentences.en: I'm not in the mood to cook, let's order online.

sentences.native: मैंने कल रात एक नया फ़ोन ऑर्डर किया।
sentences.roman: maiṃne kal rāt ek nayā fon orḍar kiyā.
sentences.en: I ordered a new phone last night.

sentences.native: ऑर्डर कहाँ तक पहुँचा? ट्रैक करके देखो।
sentences.roman: orḍar kahāṃ tak pahuṃchā? ṭraik karke dekho.
sentences.en: Where's the order got to? Track it and see.

sentences.native: डिलीवरी कब तक होगी?
sentences.roman: ḍilīvarī kab tak hogī?
sentences.en: When will it be delivered?

sentences.native: डिलीवरी वाला नीचे खड़ा है, पैसे दे दो।
sentences.roman: ḍilīvarī vālā nīche khaṛā hai, paise de do.
sentences.en: The delivery guy is downstairs, give him the money.

sentences.native: मेरा ऑर्डर अभी तक नहीं आया।
sentences.roman: merā orḍar abhī tak nahīṃ āyā.
sentences.en: My order still hasn't come.

sentences.native: दस मिनट में डिलीवरी! यह कैसे होता है?
sentences.roman: das minaṭ meṃ ḍilīvarī! yah kaise hotā hai?
sentences.en: Delivery in ten minutes! How does that even work?

sentences.native: ऑनलाइन सस्ता मिलता है, दुकान पर महँगा।
sentences.roman: onlāin sastā miltā hai, dukān par mahaṃgā.
sentences.en: It's cheaper online, expensive in the shop.

sentences.native: भैया, आप कितनी देर में पहुँचेंगे?
sentences.roman: bhaiyā, āp kitnī der meṃ pahuṃcheṃge?
sentences.en: How long until you get here? (to a delivery rider)

lessons.title: Paying by UPI

tip.title: अगर … तो in real life
tip.body:
- For a future 'if', Hindi often uses the **past**: अगर ओटीपी नहीं **आया**, तो… 'if the OTP doesn't come…'.
- Drop अगर and keep **तो**: नेट नहीं चल रहा **तो** कैश दे दो.
- 'Otherwise' = **वरना** / **नहीं तो**.
- Don't use होता here — that's the unreal 'if'.

new: पैसे कट गए पर पेमेंट नहीं हुआ।

sentences.native: अगर पेमेंट नहीं हुआ, तो पैसे वापस आ जाएँगे।
sentences.roman: agar pemenṭ nahīṃ huā, to paise vāpas ā jāeṃge.
sentences.en: If the payment didn't go through, the money will come back.

sentences.native: भैया, मैं यूपीआई कर देता हूँ, खुले पैसे नहीं हैं।
sentences.roman: bhaiyā, maiṃ yūpīāī kar detā hūṃ, khule paise nahīṃ haiṃ.
sentences.en: I'll pay by UPI, I haven't got change.

sentences.native: पेमेंट हुआ? मुझे मैसेज नहीं आया।
sentences.roman: pemenṭ huā? mujhe maisej nahīṃ āyā.
sentences.en: Did the payment go through? I didn't get a message.

sentences.native: पैसे कट गए पर पेमेंट नहीं हुआ, अब क्या करूँ?
sentences.roman: paise kaṭ gaye par pemenṭ nahīṃ huā, ab kyā karūṃ?
sentences.en: The money's gone but the payment failed — what do I do now?

sentences.native: अगर ओटीपी नहीं आया, तो दोबारा कोशिश करना।
sentences.roman: agar oṭīpī nahīṃ āyā, to dobārā koshish karnā.
sentences.en: If the OTP doesn't come, try again.

sentences.native: पेमेंट हो जाए तो स्क्रीनशॉट भेज देना।
sentences.roman: pemenṭ ho jāe to skrīnshoṭ bhej denā.
sentences.en: Once the payment goes through, send me a screenshot.

sentences.native: इंटरनेट नहीं चल रहा तो कैश दे दो।
sentences.roman: inṭarneṭ nahīṃ chal rahā to kaish de do.
sentences.en: If the internet's not working, just pay cash.

sentences.native: स्कैन करके पेमेंट कर दो, कैश नहीं चलेगा।
sentences.roman: skain karke pemenṭ kar do, kaish nahīṃ chalegā.
sentences.en: Scan and pay — cash won't do.

sentences.native: जल्दी पेमेंट करो, वरना ऑर्डर कैंसल हो जाएगा।
sentences.roman: jaldī pemenṭ karo, varnā orḍar kainsal ho jāegā.
sentences.en: Pay quickly, or the order will get cancelled.

sentences.native: अगर तुम यूपीआई करोगे, तो दस रुपये कम लगेंगे।
sentences.roman: agar tum yūpīāī karoge, to das rupaye kam lageṃge.
sentences.en: If you pay by UPI, it'll be ten rupees less.

sentences.native: उसकी नई रील देखी? बहुत मज़ेदार है!
sentences.roman: uskī naī rīl dekhī? bahut mazedār hai!
sentences.en: Seen her new reel? It's hilarious!

sentences.native: मुझे फ़ॉलो कर लो, मैं भी तुम्हें फ़ॉलो कर लूँगी।
sentences.roman: mujhe folo kar lo, maiṃ bhī tumheṃ folo kar lūṃgī.
sentences.en: Follow me and I'll follow you back.

sentences.native: मैंने तुम्हारी पोस्ट पर कमेंट किया था।
sentences.roman: maiṃne tumhārī posṭ par kamenṭ kiyā thā.
sentences.en: I commented on your post.

sentences.native: उसने मेरी पोस्ट लाइक की!
sentences.roman: usne merī posṭ lāik kī!
sentences.en: She liked my post!

sentences.native: यह फ़ोटो स्टोरी पर मत लगाना, प्लीज़!
sentences.roman: yah foṭo sṭorī par mat lagānā, plīz!
sentences.en: Please don't put this photo on your story!

sentences.native: यह रील ग्रुप में शेयर करो।
sentences.roman: yah rīl grup meṃ sheyar karo.
sentences.en: Share this reel in the group.

sentences.native: उसने मुझे फ़ॉलो करना बंद कर दिया।
sentences.roman: usne mujhe folo karnā band kar diyā.
sentences.en: He stopped following me.

sentences.native: इतने कमेंट! क्या बात है!
sentences.roman: itne kamenṭ! kyā bāt hai!
sentences.en: So many comments! Amazing!

sentences.native: मैंने कल रात एक रील बनाई और अभी तक सिर्फ़ दो लाइक आए।
sentences.roman: maiṃne kal rāt ek rīl banāī aur abhī tak sirf do lāik āye.
sentences.en: I made a reel last night and so far it has got only two likes.
